dish: Wok-fried Hokkien prawn mee with thick noodles, bee hoon & sambal
address: Chomp Chomp Food Centre, 20 Kensington Park Road, S557269
w: A Michelin Plate stall and Chomp Chomp's most famous name — thick yellow noodles and bee hoon fried with prawns and squid in a prawn stock simmered for hours, finished with a dollop of sambal. The go-to plate at Serangoon Gardens' legendary supper hawker centre.

dish: Charcoal-grilled chicken, mutton & prawn satay with peanut sauce
address: Chomp Chomp Food Centre, 20 Kensington Park Road, S557269
w: One of two Chomp Chomp stalls listed in the MICHELIN Guide with a Michelin Plate — skewers grilled over charcoal to order, a supper-time institution best eaten late at Serangoon Gardens with a plate of BBQ chicken wings alongside.

dish: Orh luak (fried oyster omelette) with plump briny oysters
address: Chomp Chomp Food Centre, 20 Kensington Park Road, S557269
w: The standout orh luak of Chomp Chomp — eggs and starch fried until charred and crisp at the edges around plump, briny oysters, drizzled with tangy chilli. A perennial pick across the centre's food-guide round-ups.

dish: Charcoal BBQ chicken wings
address: Chomp Chomp Food Centre, #01-29, 20 Kensington Park Road, S557269
w: Chicken wings are practically Chomp Chomp's mascot, and Good Luck (Stall 29) grills some of the most sought-after — burnished, charred-edged skin over juicy meat, at roughly S$1.30 a wing. A supper staple of the Serangoon Gardens crowd.

dish: Sambal BBQ stingray on banana leaf
address: Chomp Chomp Food Centre, 20 Kensington Park Road, S557269
w: Chomp Chomp's best sambal BBQ seafood — fresh, flaky stingray blanketed in an addictive sambal and grilled on a banana leaf (from S$12 for a small), plus BBQ sotong and cockles. A late-night favourite that draws its own queue.

dish: Bee hoon in satay peanut gravy with cuttlefish, prawns & tau pok
n: Ang Sar Lee Satay Bee Hoon
address: Chomp Chomp Food Centre, 20 Kensington Park Road, S557269
w: A 40-plus-year Chomp Chomp veteran plating thin bee hoon drowned in a fragrant satay peanut gravy with cuttlefish, prawns, pork and tau pok — the Serangoon Gardens rendition of a dish few hawkers still make well.

dish: Dark, wet fried Hokkien prawn mee
address: Chomp Chomp Food Centre, 20 Kensington Park Road, S557269
w: The other half of Chomp Chomp's Hokkien mee debate — a darker, wetter plate with its own loyal supporters who rate it over Ah Hock. Between the two, Serangoon Gardens arguably has Singapore's densest Hokkien mee rivalry.

dish: Nasi lemak with fluffy coconut rice, fragrant sambal & ikan bilis
address: Serangoon Garden Market & Food Centre, 49A Serangoon Garden Way, S555945
w: The most-recommended stall in the market — a Muslim-owned nasi lemak (from S$3) built on freshly squeezed coconut milk, pandan-scented rice and a shiok sambal, with crisp ikan bilis and add-ons. Serangoon Gardens' daytime counterpoint to Chomp Chomp.

dish: Teochew braised duck rice with pig-organ sides
address: Serangoon Garden Market & Food Centre, #01-44, 49A Serangoon Garden Way, S555945
w: Rated among Singapore's best Teochew braised duck — tender, herbal braised duck over rice (from S$4) with pig's stomach soup and offal, from a decades-old recipe. Queues form before it opens.

dish: Kway chap with Teochew braised pig offal & flat rice sheets
address: Serangoon Garden Market & Food Centre, #01-21, 49A Serangoon Garden Way, S555945
w: A long-running kway chap stall (formerly Blanco Court) ladling silky flat rice sheets in braising liquor with well-stewed Teochew pig offal, braised egg and tau pok — a market breakfast institution.

dish: Roasted chicken rice
address: Serangoon Garden Market & Food Centre, 49A Serangoon Garden Way, S555945
w: A market favourite for old-school roasted and poached Hainanese chicken rice, repeatedly singled out across the Serangoon Garden Market food-guide round-ups.

dish: Old-school curry buns, coconut buns & cream puffs from S$1.10
address: Serangoon Garden Market & Food Centre, #01-45/46, 49A Serangoon Garden Way, S555945
w: A 40-year neighbourhood bakery baking from 2am — classic coconut, cream-puff, chicken-sausage and curry buns from S$1.10, all made from scratch. A generational fixture inside the market.

dish: Fried oyster omelette (orh luak)
address: Serangoon Garden Market & Food Centre, 49A Serangoon Garden Way, S555945
w: A veteran orh luak stall frying crisp, starchy oyster omelettes to order — one of the market's most-named stalls in the food-guide coverage of Serangoon Garden.

dish: Teochew fishball & mushroom minced-meat noodles
n: Lao Song Fa (Botanical Garden Famous Fishball Noodle)
address: Serangoon Garden Market & Food Centre, 49A Serangoon Garden Way, S555945
w: An old-name fishball noodle stall carrying the 'Botanical Garden Famous' lineage — springy mee pok tossed with handmade fishballs, fishcake and minced pork, a market staple for decades.

dish: Hae mee (prawn noodle soup)
address: Serangoon Garden Market & Food Centre, 49A Serangoon Garden Way, S555945
w: A market prawn-noodle mainstay, its rich prawn-and-pork broth a recurring recommendation in the Serangoon Garden Market guides.

dish: Hum ji beng (fried dough fritters) & traditional pastries
address: Serangoon Garden Market & Food Centre, Stall 12, 49A Serangoon Garden Way, S555945
w: An old-school snack stall for hum ji beng, traditional pastries and kueh — the kind of nostalgic bite the Serangoon Garden Market food guides keep flagging.

dish: Min jiang kueh (peanut pancake) & hum ji beng
address: Serangoon Garden Market & Food Centre, #01-25, 49A Serangoon Garden Way, S555945
w: A long-standing stall for min jiang kueh (folded peanut pancake) and hum ji beng (from about S$1.30) — a market breakfast and tea-time regular.

dish: Handmade Teochew soon kueh, png kueh & gu chye kueh
address: Kovan 209 Market & Food Centre, #01-17, 209 Hougang Street 21, S530209
w: A decades-old stall hand-making Teochew kueh — soon kueh, png kueh and gu chye kueh at around S$1 each, using only fresh fillings. A Kovan 209 heritage name.

dish: Old-school Hainanese curry rice with pork chop & cabbage
address: Kovan 209 Market & Food Centre, #01-25, 209 Hougang Street 21, S530209
w: The lunch-hour queue of Kovan 209 — a heaped plate of Hainanese-style chye png flooded with curry, braise and pork gravies, with fried pork chop and cabbage. Old-school comfort food.

dish: Fried Hokkien mee, fried oyster & carrot cake
address: Kovan 209 Market & Food Centre, #01-30, 209 Hougang Street 21, S530209
w: A three-in-one stall doing moist, well-coated Hokkien mee in a velvety prawn stock (about S$3.50), plus fried oyster and white/black carrot cake with eggy bits and preserved radish.

dish: Soy-sauce wanton mee
address: Kovan 209 Market & Food Centre, #01-57, 209 Hougang Street 21, S530209
w: A decades-old wanton mee stall with a constant queue for simple, honest bowls of springy noodles in soy sauce with char siew and wantons.

dish: Wanton egg noodles with well-charred char siew
address: Kovan 209 Market & Food Centre, 209 Hougang Street 21, S530209
w: A community-loved wanton mee for its well-charred char siew and springy egg noodles — one of Kovan 209's most cited noodle stalls.

dish: Teochew fishball noodles, dry or laksa broth
address: Kovan 209 Market & Food Centre, 209 Hougang Street 21, S530209
w: Fishball noodles with a choice of dry, soup or a coconutty, mildly spicy laksa broth, topped with fishcake, minced meat and braised mushroom — a Kovan 209 regular.

dish: Hainanese chicken rice & Nonya zi char
address: 59 Serangoon Garden Way, S555955
w: A Serangoon Gardens institution since 1983 — the Hainanese founders opened a chicken rice stall, then hired a Nonya chef, and today it is rated among Singapore's best traditional Hainanese chicken rice with a Peranakan zi char spread.

dish: Roti prata, roti tsunami, maggi mee goreng & teh tarik towers
address: 1 Kensington Park Road, S557253
w: The 24-hour prata and mamak institution of Serangoon Gardens, famed for crispy plain prata, the over-the-top 'roti tsunami', chocolate prata and maggi mee goreng — its R.K. Special once a Sunday Times 'Cheap & Good' pick.

dish: 24-hour roti prata & maggi goreng with drink towers
address: 56 Serangoon Garden Way, S555952
w: A 24-hour prata house that gave R.K. its cross-street rival — prata, murtabak and maggi goreng served with massive drink towers, a Serangoon Gardens supper staple.

dish: Mediterranean-leaning brunch & softserve
address: 65 Serangoon Garden Way, S555961
w: A long-running Serangoon Gardens cafe from the Atlas Coffeehouse / Columbus Coffee team — minimalist interiors, a solid brunch menu and a cult dark-chocolate-and-miso-caramel softserve. The area's flagship specialty-coffee address.

dish: Charcoal Teochew fish head steamboat
n: Tian Wai Tian Fish Head Steamboat
address: 203 Hougang Street 21, #01-89, S530203
w: A tiny, wildly popular Kovan streetside zi char serving Teochew-style fish head steamboat in traditional charcoal aluminium pots — pomfret, red grouper or bighead carp — plus salted-egg pork ribs and prawn-paste chicken. Usually packed out by 5.30pm.

dish: Chinese-style nasi lemak with crispy chicken wing
address: 965 Upper Serangoon Road, S534721
w: The perennial after-midnight queue on Upper Serangoon Road is a Kovan landmark in itself. Founded 1979 (by the eldest of the Koh nasi lemak family), it's iconic for Chinese-style coconut rice with super-crispy chicken wings, luncheon meat and fried egg.

dish: Peppery Thai-style kway chap with curled rice sheets
address: 945 Upper Serangoon Road, S534711
w: A Kovan casual restaurant doing a distinctive Thai take on kway chap — a light, peppery broth (milder than bak kut teh) with silky, curled rice sheets and Thai-style braised sides, open till 3am for the supper crowd.

dish: Handcrafted ice cream & waffles till 2am
address: 957 Upper Serangoon Road, S534717
w: A late-night Kovan dessert cafe open until 2am, pairing crisp waffles with handcrafted ice cream in offbeat flavours — a viral-friendly stop on the Upper Serangoon supper strip.

dish: 24/7 roti prata, murtabak & maggi goreng
address: Hougang Village, 681 Hougang Avenue 8, #01-855, S530681
w: The mainstay 24/7 mamak for Kovan and Hougang residents — plain prata about S$2.60 for two, egg prata, murtabak and teh tarik at any hour. A Hougang-edge supper anchor.

dish: Sourdough, salted-caramel cube croissant & baguettes
address: Space @ Kovan, 9 Yio Chu Kang Road, #01-54, S545523
w: An artisanal bakery-cafe on the Kovan edge known for freshly baked sourdough, baguettes and a viral salted-caramel cube croissant — a modern counterpoint to the neighbourhood's old-school bakes.

dish: Specialty coffee, jaffles & brunch
address: 730 Upper Serangoon Road, #01-01, Singapore
w: A well-loved Kovan brunch cafe for specialty coffee and toasted jaffles in a light, plant-filled space — it closed on 19 Jan 2025. Kept here as a flagged closure.
